method: Record first. Analysis second. Hypothesis labelled. Missing record shown.
boundary: Inclusion means public-record research relevance. It does not prove wrongdoing, secret control, criminal conduct, shared intent, or conspiracy.

conclusions.title: Power is routed through systems
conclusions.text: The strongest useful reading is not one throne but a stack of finance, policy, law, institutions, standards, platforms, foundations, universities, contractors, media routes and jurisdictions.
conclusions.proves: The site can map public routes and documented relationships across those layers.
conclusions.suggests: Long-term direction can continue through institutions and implementation channels even when visible leaders change.
conclusions.missing: Decision records, funding trails, contracts, filings, regulator records and meeting calendars.

conclusions.title: Centralisation lanes are the main signal
conclusions.text: The most important lanes to track are digital identity, payment rails, AI and data governance, health-security systems, climate compliance, platform speech rules, emergency powers and cross-border enforcement.
conclusions.proves: These lanes are concrete policy and infrastructure categories that can be sourced and tracked.
conclusions.suggests: Separate systems may become interoperable through identity, money, access, compliance and enforcement rules.
conclusions.missing: Laws, standards, vendor contracts, procurement records, regulator guidance and opt-out rules.

conclusions.title: Influence often begins before law
conclusions.text: Policy usually starts upstream: reports, funders, think tanks, expert panels, corporate lobbying, consultations, standards bodies and media framing before it becomes law or practice.
conclusions.proves: The route can be investigated with public records.
conclusions.suggests: Agenda-setting can matter as much as final votes.
conclusions.missing: Report citations, funder disclosures, consultation records, lobbying filings and meeting calendars.

conclusions.title: Jurisdiction is an operating layer
conclusions.text: Courts, registries, tax systems, treaty seats, arbitration venues, trust law and corporate-law centres are not background details. They are where power is stored, moved and protected.
conclusions.proves: Jurisdictional routes can be mapped with public records.
conclusions.suggests: Legal geography is a major part of elite operating power.
conclusions.missing: Company records, court filings, beneficial ownership records, trust records and treaty texts.

conclusions.title: Accountability needs hard records
conclusions.text: The strongest public-interest investigations should be built from court records, regulator actions, sanctions, settlements, procurement disputes, disclosures, filings and missing-record tasks.
conclusions.suggests: Weak claims should become evidence hunts instead of being published as certainty.
conclusions.missing: Dockets, enforcement notices, settlement documents, procurement files and official reports.

conclusions.title: Hidden-hand interpretation stays labelled
conclusions.text: The site can examine older elite networks, symbolic systems, fraternal history, dynastic continuity and centralisation patterns as an interpretation lane, but it must label that lane clearly.
conclusions.proves: The site can track historical and public-record relevance.
conclusions.suggests: Symbolic and historical frameworks may help readers interpret recurring patterns.
conclusions.missing: Primary texts, archives, membership records, correspondence, funding records and direct influence documents.

tasks: Attach every major person card to institutions, roles, filings and source records.
Attach every policy card to legal text, consultation records, implementation dates and affected clocks.
Attach every think tank card to funders, reports, citations and policy outcomes.
Attach every jurisdiction card to registries, laws, courts, treaty roles and money routes.
Turn unsupported claims into missing-record tasks instead of final claims.
Remove internal production notes and convert them into reader-safe method notes or operator-only reports.
